entries.rationale: The finite-set complements, symmetric difference, cardinality bounds, and sums are fully specified symbolically; the ordered-pair count does not depend on a diagram.
The definition of B_n and the minimization of its distinct values are an algebraic finite-case problem; a visual representation is not needed to determine k or the smallest element.

The operation is defined by complements and set differences on a six-element universe, and the choices ask which identities and a count are correct; a set diagram can organize membership cases, but direct set algebra is sufficient.
